div.p: In Soft Real-Time (SRT) or Hard Real-Time (HRT) applications, the behaviour of the computing system must be predictable at design phase because it impacts on the design itself. Nowadays, hardware architectures are able to provide higher performance and guarantee temporal determinism but few works investigate the computational effort required by control algorithms implementation. This preliminary work aims to be a first step towards a novel analysis of performances and Worst-Case Execution Time (WCET) which can be useful to compare different control techniques and for evaluating also the complexity of the algorithms. To this purpose, a mobile robot consisting of motorized cart-pendulum has been built and it has been equipped with an HRT hardware platform where a nonlinear State Dependent Riccati Equation (SDRE) technique has been implemented.

div.head: I. INTRODUCTION
div.p: Nowadays, industrial automation systems or autonomous systems, can incorporate more sensors and more powerful controllers. Moreover, the SRT or HRT nature of these kind of systems makes it crucial that future architectures are able to provide higher performance and guarantee temporal determinism, especially regarding Industry 4.0 issues [1] [2]. Therefore, the behaviour of the computing system must be predictable at design phase and the need of predictability has significant impacts on the design itself [3]. In order to satisfy these temporal constrains and guarantee correctly working of the system, research on timing analysis of Real Time (RT) systems started many years ago and has have been focused on the Response Time Analysis (RTA) [4], [5]. However, it is still difficult to analyse a real system using those methods because of the unpredictable randomness of the CPU which cannot be accurately modelled. Because of these lack, nowadays, HRT requirements are solved via hardware, using multicores embedded boards that allows the computation of the deterministic execution time. The availability of this embedded architecture, has encouraged the designers to define new ways to evaluate control algorithms efficiency, not only analysing performances but also evaluating a tight WCET of the control algorithms implementation. Indeed, this area still lacks of deeply investigations. Very few works have been devoted to the implementation and performance evaluation of control algorithms on deterministic multi-core platforms [6] and there are no works focused on the control algorithms analysis from the point of view of performances and deterministic execution time needed. This assertion is especially valid for nonlinear controls, which typically requires even more computation effort and strict determinism for real time applications. This preliminary work aims to be a first step towards a novel analysis of performances and WCET useful to compare further different control techniques and for evaluating also the algorithms complexity. To this purpose, a mobile robot consisting of motorized four-wheeled cart-pendulum has been built with an inverted pendulum on the top and it has been equipped with an HRT hardware platform where a nonlinear SDRE controller has been implemented. The preliminary results obtained are encouraging and the possibility of evaluating new features to improve the choice amongst various control techniques may turn out very helpful. This especially in recent applications such as cyber physical systems, where the execution time taken by the control algorithm must be known at the design stage to guarantee performances in the Factories of the Future [7] [8] [9].

div.head: IV. PRELIMINARY RESULTS
div.p: In this section preliminary results regarding the cartpendulum system controlled by SDRE algorithm are presented. In the following are reported the results of the tests carried out to proof the model consistency, by comparing simulation and experimental behaviour, to validate the control algorithm design and implementation as well as also to show first results obtained from the novel WCET analysis.

div.head: A. Hardware set-up
div.p: The hardware platform which has been used in this work is the XMOS XK-1A. This board comprises a single XS1-L1 device, 128KBytes SPI FLASH memory, hosts four deterministic cores operating at 100Mhz and 64 KBytes of on-chip RAM. Amongst various types of HRT board, this was satisfying for the purposes because provides parallel computing allowing to distribute the tasks of our control application among dedicated cores. This architecture gives determinism to the operations; this feature have been efficiently used to the estimation of the Best Case Scenario (BCS) and Worst Case Scenario (WCS), related to the control tasks. In particular, the WCS can provide an upper-bound limit to consider the WCET and set the upper temporal limit of the application. This feature, as explained in the introduction Section, can be very useful, in SRT and even more in HRT applications, where temporal deadlines cannot be missed. To conclude the hardware set-up list, the YUMO E6A2-CWZ3E Rotary Encoder sensor has been used for the measure of the pendulum angle while the HC-SR04 ultrasonic distance sensor for precise cart distance measurements (up to about 3 meters) from the reference obstacle. Finally, four DC motors are operated by the shared output voltage provided by a sabertooth system which is driven by a PWM signal generated by the XK-1A board via software and the whole system is powered by a 12V battery pack. This prototype developed by the authors is presented in Figure 1.

div.head: B. Simulation and Experimental results
div.p: The cart-pendulum is evaluated for control regulation tasks, indeed, the system must maintain the pendulum in upright position (φ = 0) while maintaining a desired distance from the wall (x), measured by the sonar. In Figure 2 the real angle and the simulated angle φ of the cart-pendulum provided by SDRE controller are presented. In Figure 3 the real position and the simulated position x are presented and lastly in Figure 4 the control input U in both cases are compared. As is possible to see in Figure 2, the controller is able to satisfy regulation task by maintaining the φ angle and the x position (Fig. 3) close to the reference values, unless small oscillations. Moreover, in all the three figures the trends are very similar, except for the small deviations of the simulated results when robot changes direction (peaks) which may be attributed to the not perfect modelling of the tyre-road contact point (slip condition). However, focusing on Figure 4 the control input U almost matches for both cases which means to have a correct controller algorithm design and implementation in the HRT board.

div.head: C. WCET analysis results
div.p: Using the XMOS HRT board is possible to run independently each task to evaluate the execution time required by each one. More in detail, in our implementation the first core manages the gathering of data from the position sensor. The second core manages the gathering of data from the encoder used for the feedback of pendulum angle. Then, both cores are responsible of making available the respective data, through the respective channel, managed by the third core. This latter retrieves the sensor data from the correspondent channel every 20ms, time within the running task on the third core must compute the control law and send the message to the task 4 running on core fourth which generates the PWM to drive the motors. All these tasks are run in parallel in the HRT board and their execution time is computed statically by means of the TimeAnalyzer, a feature provided by the development environment of XMOS. Here, it has been calculated for each running task the BCS and WCS. These features are extremely helpful in application where the time is a fundamental requirement. In table III, are listed the values in ms for the described running tasks. These preliminary results give an idea on the algorithm complexity and on its temporal upper bound, to set a consistent sampling time k for the application and to quantify in term of time the computational effort required by a nonlinear controller. V. CONCLUSION In this paper the first step towards the implementation on embedded HRT device of discrete SDRE nonlinear optimal control technique has been carried out with encouraging perspectives. The authors experienced the effectiveness expressed by the deterministic parallel hardware platform, which allows the control designer to operate at higher level and have new features to improve the choice amongst various available control techniques. In particular, the BCS and the WCS of each different task required to stabilize the pendulum in the vertical position are evaluated. The results obtained are interesting and further future investigation will be devoted to evaluate more complex regulation tasks.
